justify_why_gaps_are_missing.justification: The x-axis uses a logarithmic-like tick spacing (e.g., 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10) but there are additional data points plotted at 0% as a separate vertical column at the far left. This indicates a discontinuity to accommodate zero values on a log-scaled axis, yet there are no standard visual axis-break markers (zigzag or oblique break marks) to indicate the omitted interval.

The y-axis displays log-scaled ticks (e.g., 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100) while zero-frequency points are shown separately along the bottom (a row of points at 0%). This implies a gap between zero and the smallest plotted positive value on the log scale, but no conventional axis-break indicator (diagonal/zigzag marks) is present to denote the discontinuity.
